auth.sessions: Backend owns User/AuthSession, per-installation token families, refresh rotation/replay detection, revocation and multi-device lifecycle.

multiDevice.isolation: A compromised/replayed refresh token revokes the affected session/token family by default, not every device.

installationBinding.flutter: Generate one random installation identifier on first launch, store it in OS-backed secure storage, and send X-Installation-Id on login/refresh and authenticated requests.
installationBinding.web: Backend owns a persistent HttpOnly installation cookie separate from access/refresh cookies; normal logout does not delete it.
installationBinding.note: IP/User-Agent changes are risk signals, not proof of identity or compromise.

refreshSafety.frontendRule: Serialize refresh attempts per installation (single-flight/mutex). Never branch refresh-token chains client-side.

backendOwns: Provider token verification and Fable session issuance.
Apple server credentials/private key when Apple is enabled.
clientMustDo: Use the platform provider SDK/OAuth flow to obtain the Google ID token or Apple identity token + authorization code required by Fable.
Send provider credentials only to Fable social-auth endpoints; do not create a parallel Firebase Auth account authority.

frontendRules: Never treat an email match from Google/Apple as permission to auto-link an existing Fable account.
If backend returns AUTH_SOCIAL_LINK_REQUIRED, prove ownership of the existing account, then call the explicit link flow.
Flutter must persist one random Installation ID in secure storage and send X-Installation-Id; do not use IMEI/MAC/serial-number fingerprinting.
Use a refresh mutex/single-flight per installation. A rotated refresh token must never be reused to mint a second branch.

distinctions.applePay: Wallet/payment method for ordinary merchant payments. It is not Apple App Store in-app billing.
distinctions.appleAppStore: Store billing for qualifying digital goods/subscriptions in iOS. Server verifies signed store data.
distinctions.googlePay: Wallet/payment method for ordinary merchant payments. It is not Google Play Billing.
distinctions.googlePlay: Store billing for qualifying digital goods/subscriptions in Android. Backend re-checks authoritative Play API state.

backendOwns: Final payable amount, currency and immutable financial snapshot. Client application never supplies an authoritative price.
Provider secrets, webhook/JWS verification, replay protection, ledger posting, reconciliation, refunds/approvals and financial audit.
Business-facing verified financial events. Provider adapters never call Orders/Bookings/Memberships directly.
clientMustDo: Render methods returned by backend/configuration; do not hard-code enabled payment methods.
Never collect or forward raw PAN/CVV when a hosted/tokenized provider flow is available.
Treat redirect/success-screen/client callback as UI only; never unlock business value until backend reports verified financial state.
Cash/bank/exchange/manual flows remain pending until backend evidence/approval/reconciliation confirms collection.
For Apple Pay vs App Store and Google Pay vs Play Billing, use the correct flow described by the client contract instead of treating them as synonyms.
adminSurfaces: Overview / financial summary / monthly-yearly trends / previous-period comparison
Provider accounts and connection mode (sandbox/live/deferred), health and secret rotation
Settlements, provider fees, reconciliation and payout confirmation workflows
Crypto payment evidence and store-billing verification
Ledger, Trial Balance, Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, outstanding aging, inventory/valuation snapshots and period close
Risk/fraud review, webhook health, immutable financial audit and legal/compliance review status

adminViews.advanced: Accounting, reconciliation, settlement, risk and reporting.
adminViews.technical: Provider/webhook/health/configuration details without revealing saved secrets.

backendOwns: Firebase Admin SDK credentials (ADC/service account) — never send them to Web/Flutter.
Sending notifications, invalid-token cleanup, session-to-push binding and disabling registrations on logout/delete.
clientMustDo: Initialize Firebase client SDK for FCM only; Fable remains the authentication authority.
Request notification permission when required by the OS/browser.
After a Fable AuthSession exists, obtain the FCM registration token and POST it to /push/devices.
On FCM token refresh, register the new token against the same active Fable session.
When logout response asks for DELETE_LOCAL_PUSH_TOKEN, delete the local FCM token.

ios: Wait for APNs token before FCM calls when required.

web: Use the public Firebase web config.
Pass the VAPID public key to getToken().
Configure a Firebase messaging service worker for background notifications.

backendOwns: Storage driver selection (local/s3/hybrid), storage credentials, object keys and at-rest encryption policy.
Upload-session lifecycle, server-authoritative progress, resumable offsets, abandoned-upload cleanup, S3 multipart presigning/completion and private-access URLs.

Optimized-primary image storage: JPEG/PNG may be replaced by a smaller WebP primary only when the configured savings threshold is met; dimensions stay unchanged by default, and no original+optimized duplicate is stored.

Large uploads: prepare returns resumable strategy, maxParallelParts and progress; S3-compatible uploads use Presigned Multipart and the client acknowledges each part with ETag+sizeBytes. abortEndpoint cancels immediately; idle sessions are cleaned by bounded retention maintenance; Scheduled Tasks is primary when installed and HTTP is fallback.
Secure Media authorization: owning domain evaluates OWNER/ROLE/PERMISSION/MEMBERSHIP/SUBSCRIPTION/PURCHASE/INVITATION/CUSTOM policy, then issues a short-lived Authorization Grant.
Playback Session creation/revocation and Short-lived access/license tokens. Logout/session revocation invalidates playback sessions.
Multi-DRM orchestration for protected audio/video using CMAF + MPEG Common Encryption and an external DRM/KMS provider; content keys never go to frontend.
clientMustDo: Call POST /media/uploads/prepare with kind, purpose, filename, MIME, size and PUBLIC/PRIVATE visibility. Never choose Local/S3 in frontend; follow upload.strategy.
For LOCAL_RESUMABLE render backend progress.percentage and resume from nextOffsetBytes. For S3_MULTIPART upload limited parallel parts and acknowledge ETag+sizeBytes per part.
If user cancels, call abortEndpoint immediately; idle abandoned sessions are cleaned by backend retention maintenance in bounded batches; Scheduled Tasks is primary when installed.
Do not expect stored thumbnail/optimized variants; Fable stores original media only.

Protected playback: obtain an Authorization Grant from the owning domain, POST /media/:id/playback, keep the returned Playback Session id, and refresh Short-lived access/license tokens through the session. Short-lived token does NOT mean the video expires.
Send media authorization in headers/signed cookies where supported. Query tokens are disabled by default because URLs leak into history/logs/referrers.
Web: do not claim screen-recording prevention. Use EME/Multi-DRM for encrypted video; UI anti-download controls are only friction.
Android: apply FLAG_SECURE/secure surface for protected screens. iOS: observe capture state and pause/cover content; use FairPlay for encrypted media.
Honor dynamic session watermark instructions without creating a stored duplicate of the media.

If the product domain later implements Stories/Reels or another sequential-media UX, keep its feed metadata in the normal client/project cache, prefetch the next playable item, reuse the player, and refresh playback authorization in the background. Fable does not generate a Stories feature here.

When Redis/Valkey is installed, Playback Session hot state is cached briefly and invalidated on revoke/logout to reduce repeated MySQL reads. Redis/Valkey is not a video buffer and Fable never caches raw media bytes there.
developerMustKnow: Secure Media is generic and not tied to courses or purchases.
Never implement custom media cryptography. Use vetted DRM/KMS providers and standard CMAF/MPEG-CENC workflows.
Content keys, storage secrets and signing secrets are backend-only.
A camera pointed at a screen cannot be prevented by software; watermarking/detection is deterrence and traceability, not absolute prevention.
